section.subsection: As used in this rule, "appointed legislator" means:an incumbent legislator appointed to replace another legislator who resigns or is unable to serve; oran individual appointed to replace a legislator who resigns or is unable to serve.

subsection.subsection: A legislator wishing to introduce a bill or resolution shall file a request for legislation with the Office of Legislative Research and General Counsel within the time limits established by this rule.

The request for legislation shall:designate the chief sponsor, who is knowledgeable about and responsible for providing pertinent information as the legislation is drafted; andinclude drafting instructions for the legislation.
The chief sponsor of a resolution shall ensure that the drafting instructions provided under Subsection (2)(b)(ii) comply with JR4-1-204.

The chief sponsor may modify the drafting instructions provided under Subsection (2)(b)(ii) only if the modified drafting instructions do not deviate from the core subject matter of the original drafting instructions.
The Office of Legislative Research and General Counsel shall apply the standard described in Subsection (2)(d)(i)(A) in a manner that favors the chief sponsor.

If the chief sponsor wishes to modify the drafting instructions in a manner prohibited under Subsection (2)(d)(i), the chief sponsor shall file a new, separate request for legislation in accordance with this rule.

If a legislator files a request for a constitutional joint resolution, the Office of Legislative Research and General Counsel may file, on the legislator's behalf, a separate request for a bill that addresses statutory changes necessary to implement the constitutional joint resolution, if applicable.
Any legislator may file a request for legislation beginning 60 days after the Legislature adjourns its annual general session sine die.

A legislator-elect may file a request for legislation beginning on:the day after:for a single county race, the date on which the county election canvass is completed; orfor a multi-county race, the date on which the statewide election canvass is completed; orif the legislator-elect's election results have not been finalized as of the canvass date, the day after the date the election results for the legislator-elect's race are finalized.

An incumbent legislator may not file any requests for legislation as of the date that the legislator:fails to file to run for election to a seat in the Legislature;is ineligible to be included on the ballot for the election in which the legislator would have sought an additional term; orfails to win reelection and the legislator's opponent is eligible to file a request for legislation under Subsection (3)(b).

Subsection (3)(c)(i) does not apply to a request for legislation for:a general session that occurs while the legislator is in office; ora special session that occurs while the legislator is in office.

Except as provided in Subsection (3)(e), if a legislator who filed a request for legislation is unable to serve in the next annual general session for any reason, the former legislator may seek another legislator to assume sponsorship of the former legislator's legislation.

If a former legislator is unable to find another legislator to assume sponsorship under Subsection (3)(d)(i), the Office of Legislative Research and General Counsel shall abandon each request the earlier of:30 days after the day on which the former legislator is unable to serve; ornoon on the 11th day of the annual general session.
The 30-day time period described in Subsection (3)(d)(ii)(A) begins the day on which a former legislator no longer holds the former legislator's seat.

If a legislator dies while in office and is the chief sponsor of one or more requests for legislation or pieces of legislation, the individual appointed to the legislator's seat may assume sponsorship of each request for legislation or piece of legislation.

If the individual appointed to the legislator's seat chooses not to assume sponsorship of one or more of the legislator's requests for legislation or pieces of legislation, the following individual shall seek another legislator to assume sponsorship of each request for legislation or piece of legislation:if the legislator was a member of the House majority caucus, the House majority leader;if the legislator was a member of the House minority caucus, the House minority leader;if the legislator was a member of the Senate majority caucus, the Senate majority leader; orif the legislator was a member of the Senate minority caucus, the Senate minority leader.

If the individual described in Subsection (3)(e)(ii) does not find a new sponsor:for a request for legislation, the Office of Legislative Research and General Counsel shall abandon the request for legislation; andfor legislation, the legislation shall be returned to the originating chamber and filed.
A legislator-elect who is an incumbent legislator may retain any requests for legislation the legislator-elect filed before the date described in Subsection (3)(b).
An appointed legislator who is an incumbent legislator may retain any requests for legislation the appointed legislator filed before assuming the seat to which the legislator is appointed.

Except as provided in Subsection (4)(c), a legislator may not file a request for legislation with the Office of Legislative Research and General Counsel after noon on the 11th day of the annual general session.

On the 11th day of the annual general session, the Office of Legislative Research and General Counsel shall make public on the Legislature's website the short title and sponsor of each request for legislation, unless the sponsor abandons the request for legislation before noon on the 11th day of the annual general session.

After the 11th day of the annual general session, a legislator may file a request for legislation only if:for House legislation, the representative makes a motion to request legislation for drafting and introduction and that motion is approved by a constitutional majority of the House; orfor Senate legislation, the senator makes a motion to request legislation for drafting and introduction and that motion is approved by a constitutional majority vote of the Senate.
The Office of Legislative Research and General Counsel shall make public on the Legislature's website the short title and sponsor of each request for legislation described in this Subsection (4)(c).

section.subsection: After a request for legislation is abandoned, a legislator may not revive the request for legislation.

A legislator wishing to obtain funding for a project, program, or entity, when that funding request does not require that a statute be enacted, repealed, or amended, may not file a request for legislation but instead shall file a request for appropriation by following the procedures and requirements of JR3-2-701.
